user_query: We are planning a Phase 3, open‑label, randomised trial of a novel CD38‑targeted monoclonal antibody in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma after 2–3 prior lines, including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor. The drug is given intravenously every 2 weeks. The trial will enrol patients across Europe, North America, and Japan. We are seeking FDA and EMA label claims and will submit to NICE for HTA. Our TPP aims to show superiority in bone pain, physical function, and fatigue, and we also need to capture treatment tolerability and peripheral neuropathy. Please generate a full COA strategy.

Based on the web searches and the provided knowledge graph evidence, I can now generate a comprehensive COA measurement strategy for this relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma Phase 3 trial.

## COA Measurement Strategy — Relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** A hypothesis-led strategy combining EORTC QLQ-C30 plus EQ-5D-5L provides the strongest regulatory foundation for CD38-targeted monoclonal antibodies based on 5 same-class comparator trials [CT-001][CT-002][CT-003][CT-004][CT-005].

**Key challenge:** The open-label design creates high bias risk for PRO claims, requiring extensive unbiased instrument selection justification per [RULE-005] and robust objective measures to support any symptom-specific claims given EMA's rejection of isatuximab PRO data due to "open-label bias" and "missing data" [RR-013].

**Recommended starting point:** EORTC QLQ-C30 as the core multidimensional instrument (used in all 5 CD38 trials [CT-001][CT-002][CT-003][CT-004][CT-005]) plus EQ-5D-5L for NICE utility assessment, grounded in [RULE-003] requirement for sensitive multidimensional HRQL measurement and [RULE-008] mandate for validated instruments with acceptable psychometric properties for the research objective.

**Critical gap:** No comparator trial captured peripheral neuropathy via FACT/GOG-NTX despite this being a TPP domain, creating precedent uncertainty for this symptom domain.

**LANGUAGE SEARCHES**
- EORTC QLQ-C30: ["Translations include all major Western, and many African and Asian languages"](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0959804906003315), approximately 170+ languages
- EORTC QLQ-MY20: ["translated into over 70 language versions"](https://www.ajmc.com/view/review-finds-eortc-qlq-my20-useful-robust-25-years-after-development/)
- EQ-5D-5L: ["translated into more than 170 languages"](https://www.cric.nu/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/EQ-5D-5L_UserGuide_2015.pdf)
- FACT/GOG-NTX: ["Available translations of the FACT/GOG-NTX can be obtained by registering"](https://www.facit.org/measures/fact-gog-ntx), specific count not provided but limited compared to EORTC instruments

## Key Observations
- EORTC QLQ-C30 demonstrated significant efficacy signals in 3 of 5 CD38 trials, with pain and physical function showing consistent improvement patterns [CT-001][CT-002][CT-003]
- EQ-5D-5L showed positive utility outcomes in both daratumumab trials where collected, supporting NICE cost-effectiveness requirements [CT-001][CT-003]
- No CD38 trial has successfully captured peripheral neuropathy through validated instruments, creating regulatory precedent uncertainty for FACT/GOG-NTX positioning [TI-004]
- Open-label bias resulted in EMA rejection of isatuximab PRO claims despite statistical significance, highlighting the critical importance of [RULE-005] justification requirements [RR-013]
- EORTC QLQ-MY20 provides MM-specific bone pain and treatment tolerability domains that align with TPP objectives but showed mixed efficacy results in CANDOR [CT-004]
- Assessment frequency varies significantly across comparators, from monthly (ICARIA-MM) to quarterly (ALCYONE), requiring protocol justification per [RULE-006][RULE-007]

## Comparator Analysis
MAIA established EORTC QLQ-C30 plus EQ-5D-5L as the foundational CD38 strategy, demonstrating significant improvements in global health status and pain domains with daratumumab combination therapy [CT-001]. ICARIA-MM confirmed QLQ-C30 sensitivity in the RRMM setting, showing significant pain, fatigue, and physical function benefits with isatuximab despite regulatory rejection due to open-label bias concerns [CT-002][RR-013]. AQUILA reinforced the QLQ-C30/EQ-5D-5L combination for subcutaneous daratumumab formulations with positive utility outcomes [CT-003]. CANDOR introduced EORTC QLQ-MY20 for myeloma-specific domains but failed to demonstrate significant disease symptom or side effect benefits, raising questions about the instrument's sensitivity in this combination setting [CT-004]. ALCYONE showed no significant PRO benefits despite using the core QLQ-C30/EQ-5D-5L instruments, suggesting that combination effects may vary by backbone therapy [CT-005]. EORTC QLQ-C30 emerges as the single instrument with the strongest comparator support for detecting treatment benefits in CD38-targeted therapy trials, particularly for the TPP domains of pain and physical function [CT-001][CT-002][CT-003].

| EUnetHTA | EQ-5D-5L | Country-specific European value sets | In candidates | Joint clinical assessment utility evidence will be insufficient for comparative effectiveness determination |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. Whether to position EORTC QLQ-C30 as the key secondary PRO endpoint given its use in all 5 CD38 trials [CT-001][CT-002][CT-003][CT-004][CT-005] and demonstrated sensitivity to pain and physical function changes, despite EMA's rejection of isatuximab PRO claims due to open-label bias concerns [RR-013].

2. Whether to include FACT/GOG-NTX for peripheral neuropathy capture given TPP requirements and FDA/EMA acceptance [TI-004], or rely on EORTC QLQ-MY20's side effects scale which has weaker neuropathy-specific content but better regulatory precedent in myeloma.

3. Assessment schedule selection between the intensive ICARIA-MM approach (every cycle D1) versus the reduced MAIA schedule (baseline plus quarterly assessments), considering [RULE-006][RULE-012] requirements for burden minimization with bi-weekly IV administration.

4. Pre-specification hierarchy for PRO endpoints to satisfy [RULE-001][RULE-002] hypothesis-led strategy requirements, particularly whether to prioritize pain response (supported by 3 positive trials) versus physical function (mixed results) as the key secondary endpoint.

5. Translation strategy for FACT/GOG-NTX in Japanese and other Asian markets given limited availability compared to EORTC instruments, versus accepting the peripheral neuropathy measurement gap until post-approval studies can address this domain.
